review: W112 preview-TGA backend route, isolated candidate only

reviewTest.result: 4 passed, 1 confirmed finding; actual candidate Flask route with synthetic local TGA fixtures

findings.evidence: With seven entries already present and the configured maximum of eight, two concurrent unique cache misses both returned 200 and left nine entries. The eviction/check/insert at candidate lines 251-254 has no lock; each request sees the pre-insert size of seven and both skip eviction.
findings.impact: The advertised item bound is not maintained under threaded Flask request concurrency. Repeated simultaneous misses can increase memory beyond the nominal cap.
findings.minimalFix: Protect lookup/eviction/insertion as one cache-lock operation, or use a bounded synchronized cache. Keep decode outside the lock if needed, then recheck before insertion and evict until size < max while holding the lock. Add this deterministic two-miss race to the candidate test.

findings.evidence: A 56-byte fixture caused 112 source bytes to be read for both cache miss and hit: _read_tga_snapshot reads the full file into memory, then _tga_path_sha256 streams the file again before responding.
findings.impact: The implementation is content-correct but duplicates full-file I/O and keeps each source snapshot in memory for the request. No maximum source size is enforced. Large concurrent files multiply transient memory and I/O.
findings.minimalFix: Document/validate a supported TGA size bound, and consider streaming hash plus a bounded spooled snapshot used by Pillow so the exact hashed bytes are the decoded bytes. Do not hash one read then reopen a mutable path for decode.

verified: Cache key includes real path and source content SHA-256, so equal-size/equal-mtime changed content is distinguished.
Image decode uses the captured raw bytes; a mutation after snapshot is detected by the post-decode hash and returns 409 without poisoning cache.
Synthetic alpha-bearing TGA preserves pixel/alpha output and returned X-Source-Bytes-SHA256 matches the decoded snapshot.
Response is image/png and exposes neither raw source bytes nor local path in body/headers.
limits: Backend route only. The Runtime11 client/header consumer and private launcher are not exercised end-to-end here.
No customer files, live server, provider, native app, or external endpoint was used.
Concurrency finding was deterministically injected at the candidate cache mapping while calling the actual candidate Flask route; no production source was changed.
